SMTO-CTX-0024 — A search of saved files asked for too much

GUID: 2eb4a1aa-31f8-4b3b-8ed9-106de53eb4ee
Slug: resource-search-window-invalid
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: ctx

What happened

  • A search through the files saved in your conversations was refused because the search words were too long or it asked for too many results at once. No files were opened or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Shorten the search to a few key words, such as part of a file name, keeping it under 256 characters. SMTO refuses searches longer than 256 characters.
  2. If a script or tool you use made this search, set it to ask for between 1 and 50 results. SMTO returns at most 50 results per search, so a larger number is refused.
  3. If you need more than 50 matches, run several narrower searches, each with different key words. Smaller searches each stay within the limit and together cover what you need.

What success looks like

  • The search returns a list of matching files instead of this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, noting where you started the search. Don't try to get around the search limits; they keep searches fast and limited to conversations you can see.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Resource discovery rejected the search because the query is not text, is longer than 256 characters, or the result limit is outside 1 to 50.

What this means

  • Resource discovery rejects a non-text or over-256-character query and any result limit outside 1 through 50. Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • Resource discovery rejects a non-text or over-256-character query and any result limit outside 1 through 50.

How to diagnose it

  • Check query length/type and requested result count; source permissions remain separate from these search bounds.

How to fix it

  • Call the context source or artifact search (GET /api/agent/context/sources or /api/agent/context/artifacts, or the matching store methods) with a text query of at most 256 characters and a limit between 1 and 50, paging with narrower queries for more results. Keep the bounded search and conversation-scope checks in place.
  • Narrow the query and choose a supported result limit without disabling bounded search.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The bounded query is accepted and returns no more than the supported result limit.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass scope or ownership checks to force a larger operation through.

Technical notes

  • Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
